# Toast

A brief, polite confirmation of something the reader just did, shown away from the content and gone on its own.

**Not implemented yet.** This page is the *approved intent* — the props API signed off at gate 1 of the build order, before any React exists. Do not import it; there is nothing to import.

| | |
|---|---|
| Registry name | `toast` |
| Family | feedback |
| Tier | free |
| Status (css / react / figma) | future / future / future |
| Depends on | `state-layer`, `icon` |

## Behavior

A message rendered into one app-level toast region, announced politely, never taking focus, and removed after `duration` unless the reader is hovering it, focused inside it, or away from the tab. The region is `ToastRegion`, mounted once near the app root, and a Toast is shown from an event handler with the `useToast()` hook — both approved at gate 1.

- **Toast confirms; Notice informs; Dialog interrupts** — A toast is for the result of something the reader just did, whose confirmation they can safely miss: "Saved", "Link copied", "Message sent". Anything the reader must see is not a toast, because a toast goes away on a timer and appears far from where they were looking. A problem with what is on the page — a validation summary, a failed save that left the form dirty — is a Notice in the page, beside the thing it is about. A decision that blocks the task is a Dialog. A toast that reports a form error is a message the reader has to hunt for, about a form it is not next to.
- **Three variants, not Notice's four, and no warning** — `neutral`, `success` and `danger`. There is no `info` because a neutral toast is already informational, and no `warning` because a warning is by definition something to act on — which is exactly what a self-dismissing message cannot carry. `danger` exists for failures that need no immediate action — "Couldn't sync, will retry" — and is the variant to question hardest at review.
- **Always polite, never assertive, and focus never moves** — The reader is mid-task, and a toast's content is by definition not urgent — urgent content is a Dialog or a Notice. So the region is a `role="status"` live region and every toast is announced politely, after whatever the screen reader is currently saying. Focus stays where the reader put it; stealing it to a corner of the screen for "Saved" would be a worse bug than missing the confirmation.
- **The timer pauses, and an action means the toast is not the only way** — WCAG 2.2.1 requires timed content to be adjustable. The countdown pauses while the pointer is over the toast, while focus is inside it, and while the tab is hidden, so a reader who is reading it, or reaching for its action, or who switched away, does not lose it. An action in a toast — Undo, View — must also be reachable somewhere else in the interface, because the toast will eventually leave; a toast whose action is the only path to something must pass `duration={null}` and stay until dismissed.
- **`ToastRegion` and `useToast()` are part of the API** — Approved at gate 1 (decision C5, docs/decisions/2026-11-gate-1-review.md). A toast is raised from an event handler — a save that finished, a path that was copied — far from where it is drawn, so rendering `<Toast>` in place would put it in whatever stacking context the handler's component happens to live in. `ToastRegion` is the one place every toast lands, mounted once near the app root; `useToast()` returns `show`, which hands a Toast to that region from anywhere below it. Toast itself stays a plain component with the props below, so the region owns the stack, the timers and the live region, and the message owns only what it says.
- **One region per app, in the top layer, stacking at most three** — Toasts from anywhere in the app have to land in one place, or two of them overlap and a screen reader hears neither cleanly. The region is a single `popover="manual"` element so it sits in the top layer without a z-index — there are no z-index tokens in this system and the top layer is why none are needed. More than three visible at once is a log, not a confirmation; the oldest leaves early to make room.
- **Web and native** — Web: each toast is a `div` inside one `role="status"` region, named "Notifications" with `aria-label` so it can be found by landmark navigation; the region carries `popover="manual"`. Icons are `aria-hidden`, as in Notice. React Native has no top layer: the region is an absolutely positioned `View` mounted once at the root, above the navigation container. Each toast sets `accessibilityLiveRegion="polite"` on Android and is announced with `AccessibilityInfo.announceForAccessibility` on iOS, where live regions do not exist; the action is `accessibilityRole="button"`. Swipe-to-dismiss is native-only, and always backed by the dismiss button, because a gesture is not discoverable by a screen reader. The pause-on-hover half of the timer rule is web-only; on native the timer pauses while a screen reader is running. Rata-drawn on both platforms, not the OS's own toast (decision N5): Android's system Toast cannot carry an action or a dismiss button, and iOS has none, so one drawn component behaves the same everywhere. The native implementation ships in the pro tier (decision N6).
- **Open question for approval: toasts while a modal Dialog is open** — `showModal()` makes everything outside the dialog inert, and whether a top-layer region opened earlier stays interactive and announced above it is something to verify in the browsers this system supports, not to assume. Until it is verified, the contract says: do not raise a toast from inside a modal; report the result inside the dialog, or after it closes.

## Props

| Prop | Type | Default | Summary |
|---|---|---|---|
| `children` | `ReactNode` | — | The message — one short sentence about what just happened. |
| `variant?` | `"neutral" \| "success" \| "danger"` | `"neutral"` | Whether the outcome says anything about health. |
| `action?` | `{ label: string; onAction: () => void }` | — | One optional action — Undo, View — offered alongside the message. |
| `duration?` | `number \| null` | `6000` | Milliseconds before the toast leaves on its own, or `null` to stay until dismissed. |
| `onDismiss?` | `() => void` | — | Called when the toast leaves — by timer, by the dismiss button, or by a swipe on native. |
| `dismissLabel?` | `string` | `"Dismiss"` | Accessible name for the dismiss button. |

### `children`

```ts
children: ReactNode
```

The message — one short sentence about what just happened.

**Use when**

- Past tense, naming the thing: "Invoice sent", "3 tokens copied".

**Don't use for**

- Anything the reader must act on, or an error about something on the page. That is a Notice, where the problem is.
- More than one sentence. It is read while it is leaving.

**Accessibility** Announced politely through the region's live region when the toast appears.

### `variant`

```ts
variant?: "neutral" | "success" | "danger" = "neutral"
```

Whether the outcome says anything about health.

**Use when**

- `neutral` for almost everything — a confirmation is not a celebration.
- `success` when the outcome was in real doubt: a long export that finished.
- `danger` for a failure that needs no action now: "Couldn't sync, will retry".

**Don't use for**

- `danger` for a failure the reader has to fix. That is a Notice beside the thing that failed.

**Accessibility** Colour is not the only signal: the success and danger variants carry an icon, as Notice does, which is `aria-hidden` because the text already says it.

### `action`

```ts
action?: { label: string; onAction: () => void }
```

One optional action — Undo, View — offered alongside the message.

**Use when**

- Undo for a reversible action the reader may have done by mistake.

**Don't use for**

- An action that is reachable nowhere else, unless `duration` is `null`. The toast will leave, and the action with it.
- Two actions. A choice between options is a Dialog.

**Accessibility** Rendered as a real button. The timer pauses while focus is inside the toast, so a keyboard user reaching for it does not lose it.

### `duration`

```ts
duration?: number | null = 6000
```

Milliseconds before the toast leaves on its own, or `null` to stay until dismissed.

**Use when**

- The default for almost everything.
- `null` when the toast's action is the only path to something.

**Don't use for**

- Shortening it. The timer already pauses on hover and focus, but a short message read by a screen reader can take longer than it looks.

**Accessibility** Paused while hovered, while focus is inside, and while the tab is hidden — the adjustment WCAG 2.2.1 requires for timed content.

### `onDismiss`

```ts
onDismiss?: () => void
```

Called when the toast leaves — by timer, by the dismiss button, or by a swipe on native.

**Use when**

- Cleaning up state that should not outlive the message.

**Don't use for**

- Treating it as "the reader saw it". A timed-out toast may have been read by nobody.

### `dismissLabel`

```ts
dismissLabel?: string = "Dismiss"
```

Accessible name for the dismiss button.

**Use when**

- A translated label.

**Don't use for**

- Removing the button. Every toast is dismissible by hand, whatever its duration.

**Accessibility** Becomes the icon-only button's `aria-label`.

## Use cases

### A confirmation that can safely be missed

The reader did something whose result is not otherwise visible where they are.

```tsx
const toast = useToast();

<Button onClick={() => { copy(path); toast.show(<Toast>Token path copied</Toast>); }}>
  Copy path
</Button>
```

Neutral, default duration, no action. `show` hands the toast to the `ToastRegion` mounted once at the app root. Focus stays on the button, and the message is announced politely after the button's own feedback.

### Undo for something reversible

A destructive action that is cheap to reverse, where confirming in advance would be friction.

```tsx
toast.show(
  <Toast action={{ label: "Undo", onAction: () => restore(row.id) }}>
    Row archived
  </Toast>
);
```

Archived rows must also be restorable from the archive itself — the toast will leave, and Undo with it. If they were not, this would need `duration={null}`.

### Reaching for the wrong component

A save that failed because two fields are invalid.

```tsx
toast.show(<Toast variant="danger">Check the highlighted fields</Toast>);
```

Don't. The reader has to act, and the problem is in the form, not in the corner of the screen. That is a Notice at the top of the form with `live="assertive"`, and the fields' own invalid status.

## Token recipe

### base

Notice's frame on a floating surface. The text, icon and dismiss are built exactly as Notice builds them, so a toast and a notice saying the same thing look like the same message; the difference is the shadow and where it sits.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| padding | `space.padding.sm space.padding.md` |
| border-radius | `radius.element` |
| box-shadow | `theme.elevation.overlay` |
| border | `border.default solid theme.border.default` |
| gap between icon, text and actions | `space.gap.sm` |
| font-size | `type.body.size` |
| line-height | `type.body.line-height` |
| icon size | `size.icon.text` |
| inline-size | `text bounded by size.measure.compact; the box is that plus its padding, never wider than the viewport less twice space.page.gutter` |
| enter transition | `motion.overlay.duration with motion.easing.enter` |
| exit transition | `motion.overlay.duration with motion.easing.exit` |

### neutral

The default, and the commonest: "Saved", "Link copied". A plain surface, because most confirmations say nothing about health.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| background | `theme.bg.surface` |
| color | `theme.fg.primary` |

### success

The role's subtle tint with its own foreground — the same pairing Notice uses.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| background | `theme.success-role.subtle` |
| color | `theme.success-role.fg` |

### danger

A failure the reader should know about but does not have to act on now. The role's subtle tint with its own foreground; never the saturated fill.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| background | `theme.danger-role.subtle` |
| color | `theme.danger-role.fg` |

### region

Where toasts stack. Fixed to the viewport's block-end edge, inset by the page's own gutter.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| inset from the viewport edges | `space.page.gutter` |
| gap between toasts | `space.stack.xs` |

### dismiss

Notice's dismiss control, unchanged.

| Property | Token |
|---|---|
| color | `currentColor — inherited from the variant's own foreground` |
| glyph size | `size.icon.text` |
| target inline-size / block-size | `size.control.sm` |
| border-radius | `radius.inner` |
| hover / press | `compose the .rata-state-layer class` |
| focus ring | `theme.focus-ring at focus.ring-width, offset focus.ring-offset, on :focus-visible` |
